cause.note: third read of the record, and the operator's governed-document rule applied to the harvest

changes.what: Third full read (eleven readers, the revision-2 document of 25 themes and 31 tensions as the lens) reported 164 rows, 26 of them the operator's, and opened no new theme of substance.
changes.why: Convergence is judged by shrinking findings (Theme 13), not a round count; the read had to run to establish that the findings had fallen to echoes.

changes.what: Folded into the body: two new tensions (32, where a governed evidence corpus may live; 33, one silent re-run versus nondeterminism-is-a-defect), the operator's #38311 under Theme 13, and three first-statement provenance corrections (#50717 before #52568; #47502 before #48930; #52034 in Tension 16).
changes.why: These are the genuinely-new items of the third read; #38311 in particular is the consequence-bounded 80/20 criterion on which the convergence verdict rests.

changes.what: The remaining ~150 third-read rows (agent-authored mechanism detail that sharpens existing themes without changing the structure or any ruling) were NOT inlined; they are preserved verbatim under docs/harvests/pass-3-reader-notes/ and named as the residue in the appendix.
changes.why: Inlining them would bloat an already-long document and skew later readers — the same cost the governed-document rule exists to prevent — while the reader notes keep them lossless and citable.

changes.what: Applied the governed-document rule: the 'Pass 2 additions' blocks were dissolved into each theme's list, the '(pass 2)' markers were removed from Part 4, and the status line and appendix no longer narrate passes.
changes.why: The body should read as a first version; this history belongs in the changelog, not in the document.

changes.what: Second read: eleven readers re-read the entire May 29 - Aug 24 record with the 21 themes and 15 tensions of read 1 as the lens, reporting only what read 1 missed. 307 rows reported; 276 kept after dedup (27 merged as supporting ids; 4 dropped as already present).
changes.why: A single-pass audit is incomplete by definition; the re-sweep tests whether the first pass's themes hold and what they missed.

changes.what: Produced four new themes (22 UX-as-standard, 23 framework parity, 24 release mechanics, 25 the constitution outlives the codebase), sixteen new tensions (16-31), and sharpened eleven existing tensions.
changes.why: The kept rows named surface the first pass had not covered.

changes.what: First read: eleven readers read the full corpus (15,419 messages across 17 topics) once, keeping every row bearing on rules, registers or glossary terms — 1,618 rows read, 602 kept. Produced the first 21 themes and 15 tensions, plus a per-document corrections list.
changes.why: To find everything in the conversation record that the three foundational documents do not yet reflect.
